name: Chocolate Protein Recovery Shake
description: A thick chocolate-banana shake with milk and protein powder. There's spinach in it, and you won't taste it.
steps: Pour the milk into the blender first so the powder doesn't stick to the bottom.
Add the protein powder, banana, spinach and ice.
Blend for 45-60 seconds until completely smooth.
Drink it within 30-60 minutes of finishing your session.
tip: About 35 g protein and 40 g carbs. After a long or very hard session, add a second banana or 2 tbsp oats to get the carbs up.

name: Greek Yogurt with Berries and Honey
description: Thick Greek yogurt with berries, honey and a little granola crunch. Two minutes from fridge to spoon.
steps: Spoon the yogurt into a bowl.
Top with the berries, then drizzle over the honey.
Scatter the granola on just before eating so it stays crunchy.
tip: A roughly 2:1 carbs-to-protein ratio. It's a good everyday recovery snack after an easy or moderate run.

name: Banana Protein Smoothie
description: A banana-bread-in-a-glass smoothie with vanilla protein, Greek yogurt, oats and cinnamon.
steps: Blitz the oats on their own for 10 seconds to a powder, so the smoothie comes out silky rather than bitty.
Add the almond milk, banana, protein powder, yogurt, honey, cinnamon and ice.
Blend for 60 seconds until smooth, then drink straight away.
tip: The oats add slow-release carbs, which makes this a good one when the next meal is a few hours away.

name: Chocolate Milk
description: Proper homemade chocolate milk with cocoa, a little sugar and a pinch of salt. One of the best-studied recovery drinks there is.
steps: In a glass or shaker, mix the cocoa, sugar and salt with 2 tbsp warm milk into a smooth paste. Cocoa clumps in cold milk.
Whisk or shake in the rest of the milk.
Drink it cold. Make it the night before and keep it in the fridge so it's waiting when you get back.
tip: Fluid, sodium and a roughly 2-3:1 carbs-to-protein ratio in one glass. Ideal when you can't face food straight after a race.

name: Protein Energy Balls
description: No-bake date, almond butter and oat balls boosted with protein powder. Keep a batch in the fridge for straight after training.
steps: If the dates are firm, soak them in hot water for 10 minutes, then drain them well.
Blitz the dates in a food processor for 1 minute to a sticky paste.
Add the almond butter, protein powder, oats, chia seeds, vanilla and salt and pulse until the mixture clumps when pinched. Add water 1 tsp at a time if it's dry, or more oats if it's wet.
Roll into 12 balls with damp hands.
Chill for 30 minutes to firm up.
tip: Two balls with a glass of milk is a quick recovery snack you can eat in the car.
storage: Keeps for 1 week in the fridge or 3 months in the freezer.

name: Cottage Cheese with Fruit
description: Cottage cheese with juicy pineapple or berries, almonds, honey and cinnamon. High in protein and ready in two minutes.
ingredients: 150 g pineapple chunks, berries or mixed fruit
steps: Spoon the cottage cheese into a bowl.
Top with the fruit and almonds.
Drizzle with the honey and dust with cinnamon.
tip: Casein-rich cottage cheese digests slowly, so it's excellent before bed after an evening session or a long day on the trails.

name: Hard-Boiled Eggs and Avocado
description: Perfectly boiled eggs with lime-smashed avocado on rye toast, finished with chilli flakes and flaky salt.
steps: Lower the eggs into boiling water and cook for 9 minutes for firm yolks that aren't chalky.
Move them into iced water for 5 minutes, then peel them under running water and halve.
Mash the avocado with the lime and a pinch of salt.
Toast the bread, spread with the avocado and top with the eggs, chilli flakes and pepper.
tip: Lower in carbs than most recovery food, so it's best after an easy run. After a hard session, add fruit or a second slice.

name: Rice Cakes with Peanut Butter
description: Crunchy rice cakes with peanut butter, banana, honey and a pinch of salt. The quickest carb top-up in the cupboard.
steps: Spread the rice cakes with the peanut butter.
Top with the banana slices.
Drizzle with honey and finish with a pinch of salt.
tip: Mostly carbs. Pair it with a glass of milk or a yogurt to reach 20 g of protein.

name: Tuna Salad Crackers
description: Zingy yogurt-mustard tuna with crunchy celery on rye crispbreads. More than 30 g of protein in under ten minutes.
ingredients: 1 tin (145 g) tuna in spring water, drained
steps: Press as much liquid out of the tuna as you can.
Mix the yogurt, mayonnaise, mustard, lemon and pepper, then fold in the tuna, celery and onion.
Pile onto the crispbreads just before eating so they stay crisp.
tip: Very high in protein. Add a piece of fruit to bring the carbs up after a long run.

name: Peanut Butter Banana Smoothie
description: A creamy classic: banana, peanut butter, milk and protein blended with ice.
ingredients: 1 scoop (30 g) vanilla or chocolate protein powder
steps: Add the milk first, then the protein powder, banana, peanut butter and ice.
Blend for 45-60 seconds until smooth.
Drink it within an hour of training.
tip: Swap the milk for a soy drink for a dairy-free version with the same protein.

name: Avocado Toast with Egg
description: Wholegrain toast with lime-smashed avocado and two runny poached or fried eggs.
steps: Poach the eggs: slide them into barely simmering water with a splash of vinegar and cook for 3 minutes. Or fry them in a non-stick pan.
Meanwhile, toast the bread.
Mash the avocado with the lime, salt and pepper and spread it over the toast.
Top with the eggs and red pepper flakes.
tip: A balanced post-run breakfast: protein, healthy fats and wholegrain carbs.

name: Almond Butter Toast with Banana
description: Wholegrain toast with almond butter, sliced banana, cinnamon and honey.
steps: Toast the bread.
Spread the almond butter right to the edges.
Top with the banana, dust with cinnamon and drizzle with honey.
tip: Carb-forward. Add a glass of milk or a yogurt for protein, or it makes a good pre-long-run breakfast 2-3 hours out.

name: Hummus and Veggie Plate
description: A snacking plate of hummus, warm pitta, a boiled egg and crunchy vegetables with a drizzle of olive oil and paprika.
ingredients: 200 g mixed vegetables (carrot, cucumber, pepper, cherry tomatoes)
steps: Boil the egg for 9 minutes, cool it in cold water and peel.
Cut the vegetables into sticks.
Warm the pitta and cut it into strips.
Spoon the hummus onto a plate, swirl it, drizzle with oil and dust with paprika. Arrange everything around it.
tip: Lots of fibre. It's great a while after training, but not right before a run.

name: Salmon and Quinoa Bowl
description: Roasted salmon on lemony quinoa with roasted Mediterranean vegetables and a Dijon herb dressing.
ingredients: 150 g courgette, pepper and red onion, in chunks
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C fan (220°C / 425°F). Roast the vegetables with 1 tsp of the oil for 25 minutes, adding the seasoned salmon to the tray for the last 12.
Meanwhile, rinse the quinoa and simmer it, covered, in the water with a pinch of salt for 12 minutes. Rest it for 5 minutes.
Whisk the remaining oil with the lemon, mustard, herbs and seasoning.
Build the bowl: quinoa, vegetables and flaked salmon, drizzled with the dressing.
tip: A complete recovery meal, with omega-3s thrown in, that also works cold as a lunch box.

name: Apple and Peanut Butter Plate
description: Crisp apple wedges with peanut butter for dipping and a glass of cold milk.
steps: Core the apple and cut it into 8 wedges.
Stir the peanut butter well (the oil separates), then spoon it into a small dish and dust with cinnamon.
Dip the apple in the peanut butter and drink the milk alongside.
tip: The milk is doing real work here: it brings the protein up to a useful recovery dose.

name: Greek Yogurt Power Bowl
description: A big bowl of protein-boosted Greek yogurt with berries, walnuts, pumpkin seeds, flaxseed and honey.
steps: Stir the protein powder into the yogurt until smooth.
Top with the berries, walnuts, pumpkin seeds and flaxseed.
Drizzle with honey and dust with cinnamon.
tip: More than 40 g of protein, which is right at the top of what muscles can use in one sitting. Ideal after heavy leg sessions.

name: Turkey and Avocado Recovery Wrap
description: Turkey, avocado, hummus and sweet chilli in a wholewheat wrap, with a banana on the side to bring up the carbs.
steps: Spread the tortilla with the hummus, then drizzle over the sweet chilli sauce.
Layer the turkey, avocado, leaves, carrot and pumpkin seeds.
Fold in the sides and roll up tightly. Cut in half.
Eat it with the banana.
tip: Pack it before a long run and eat it straight after: protein, carbs and a little fat, all in one hand.

name: Berry Recovery Smoothie Bowl
description: A thick frozen berry and cherry smoothie bowl with Greek yogurt and protein, topped with granola, hemp seeds and cacao nibs.
ingredients: 150 g frozen mixed berries and cherries
steps: Blend the frozen fruit, yogurt, protein powder and milk, stopping to scrape down the sides. Keep it thick enough to hold a spoon.
Scoop it into a bowl.
Top with the granola, hemp seeds, almond butter and cacao nibs.
tip: Cherries and berries are rich in polyphenols, which may help with soreness after hard efforts.

name: Chicken and Rice Recovery Bowl
description: The runner's staple: juicy chicken, fluffy rice and steamed vegetables with a honey-tamari drizzle and sesame.
steps: Rinse the rice and simmer it, covered, in 140 ml water for 10-12 minutes (brown rice needs 25), then rest it for 5 minutes.

Flatten the chicken slightly and season it with the garlic powder, salt and pepper. Cook it in the oil over a medium-high heat for 5-6 minutes each side until cooked through. Rest for 3 minutes and slice.
Steam the broccoli and carrot for 4 minutes.
Mix the tamari and honey with 1 tbsp water.
Build the bowl, drizzle with the sauce and sprinkle with the sesame seeds.
tip: Make four at once. It's the easiest recovery meal to batch for a big week.
storage: Keeps for 3 days in the fridge. Cool the rice quickly and reheat it until piping hot.

name: Roasted Chickpeas and Nuts
description: Crunchy smoked-paprika chickpeas tossed with mixed nuts. A savoury, plant-based snack for after easy runs.
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C fan (220°C / 425°F).
Rinse the chickpeas and dry them very thoroughly, rubbing them in a tea towel and discarding any loose skins. Moisture is what makes them chewy.
Toss with the oil, paprika, garlic powder and salt and spread them on a tray.
Roast for 25-30 minutes, shaking the tray every 10 minutes, until crunchy.
Cool on the tray (they crisp as they cool), then toss with the nuts.
tip: Low in protein for a recovery snack, so pair it with a yogurt or a glass of milk.
storage: Keeps for 3 days in an airtight tin; they soften over time.

name: 3:1 Recovery Smoothie
description: A carb-heavy recovery smoothie built on a 3:1 carbs-to-protein ratio: milk, Greek yogurt, banana, oats, berries and honey.
steps: Blitz the oats on their own for 10 seconds to a powder.
Add everything else and blend for 60 seconds until smooth.
Drink it within 45 minutes of finishing.
tip: After a long run or race, a roughly 3:1 carbs-to-protein ratio refills glycogen faster than protein alone. This one gives about 85 g carbs and 28 g protein.

name: Protein Rice Pudding
description: Creamy stovetop rice pudding with vanilla protein stirred through, topped with fruit. Warm or cold.
ingredients: 600 ml semi-skimmed milk (500 ml for cooking, 100 ml kept cold)
100 g berries or stewed apple, to serve
steps: Put the rice, 500 ml of the milk, the salt, cinnamon and vanilla in a pan and bring to a simmer.
Cook on the lowest heat for 25-30 minutes, stirring often because it catches on the bottom, until thick and creamy and the rice is soft.
Take it off the heat for 2 minutes. Whisk the protein powder into the 100 ml of cold milk until smooth, then stir it in. Powder added to boiling pudding goes grainy.
Sweeten with the maple syrup and top with the fruit.
tip: A warm recovery dessert for when a cold smoothie doesn't appeal after a race.
storage: Keeps for 3 days in the fridge. Loosen with milk when reheating.

name: Tart Cherry Recovery Smoothie
description: Montmorency tart cherry juice blended with frozen cherries, Greek yogurt, banana and protein.
ingredients: 200 ml unsweetened tart cherry juice (or 30 ml concentrate topped up with water)
steps: Add the juice to the blender first.
Add the cherries, yogurt, protein powder and banana.
Blend for 60 seconds until smooth and drink straight away.
tip: Montmorency tart cherry has some evidence for reducing muscle soreness when taken twice a day in the days around a hard race.

name: Egg Fried Rice with Peas and Edamame
description: Takeaway-style egg fried rice with peas, edamame, garlic, ginger and spring onion. Ten minutes in a hot wok.
ingredients: 300 g cold cooked rice (from about 120 g uncooked)
3 spring onions, whites and greens sliced separately
steps: Use cold rice, either day-old or cooked and chilled. Freshly cooked rice turns mushy.
Heat the oil in a wok over a very high heat. Add the eggs, scramble for 30 seconds until just set, and push them to the side.
Add the garlic, ginger and spring onion whites for 30 seconds.
Add the rice and break up any clumps. Toss for 3-4 minutes until hot and slightly toasted.
Add the peas and edamame for 2 minutes, then the soy sauce, sesame oil and spring onion greens.
tip: Add 150 g cooked prawns or chicken for an extra 25-30 g of protein after a hard session.
storage: Cool leftover rice quickly, refrigerate it within an hour, and eat it within 24 hours.

name: Bagel with Peanut Butter and Honey
description: A toasted bagel with peanut butter, banana, honey and salt, plus a glass of milk. A big-carb refuel in five minutes.
steps: Split and toast the bagel.
Spread with the peanut butter, top with the banana, drizzle with the honey and add a pinch of salt.
Drink the milk alongside.
tip: After a long run or race it refills glycogen fast. It also works as a race-morning breakfast 2-3 hours before the start; skip the milk if dairy sits badly.

name: Sweet Potato and Black Bean Quesadilla
description: Crisp tortillas filled with smoky mashed sweet potato, black beans and melted cheddar. Cut into wedges and dip in salsa.
steps: Prick the sweet potato and microwave it for 5-7 minutes until soft. Scoop out the flesh and mash it with the cumin, paprika and a pinch of salt.
Lightly crush the beans into the mash.
Spread the mixture over 2 tortillas, scatter with the cheese and top with the remaining tortillas.
Brush a frying pan with the oil and cook each quesadilla over a medium heat for 2-3 minutes each side, pressing with a spatula, until crisp and the cheese has melted.
Cut into wedges and serve with the salsa and yogurt.
tip: Plenty of carbs to refuel with. The beans make it very high in fibre, so leave a few hours before your next run.

name: Chicken and Sweet Potato Recovery Hash
description: Smoky diced chicken and crisp sweet potato with peppers, onion and spinach, topped with a fried egg. One pan.
ingredients: 250 g sweet potato, in 1.5 cm cubes
steps: Put the sweet potato in a bowl with a splash of water, cover and microwave for 4 minutes.
Heat the oil in a large frying pan over a medium-high heat. Season the chicken with the paprika and salt and cook it for 5 minutes until browned.
Add the sweet potato, onion and pepper and cook for 8 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the edges are crisp and the chicken is cooked through.
Stir in the spinach until wilted. Fry the egg alongside and put it on top.
tip: A gluten-free recovery plate with 45 g of protein. Leftovers make a good next-day lunch.
